claude_analysis.tam_assessment: The market is a small niche: Hacker News returned 1 result (8 points) and Reddit returned 10 posts, mostly students and hobbyists asking how to get into BCI, while free options such as NPTEL, Class Central and YouTube already show up in search.
claude_analysis.pricing_assessment: The only observed competitor price is $11.99 one-time (infognu.com), and coupon sites offer the same course free, so willingness to pay looks like roughly $10 per learner unless the course is repositioned as premium or B2B training.
claude_analysis.legal_reasoning: The only restriction hits were about unauthorized practice of law (westacademic.com, trtcle.com), which is unrelated to teaching BCI, and no government sources came up, so no restriction applies to selling this course.
key_risks: Expected value of about $10 per customer per year is far below the $200 acquisition floor, so paid acquisition loses money
Free substitutes (NPTEL, Class Central, YouTube, 100%-off coupons) push prices toward zero
Vendors hold 40% of search results, which limits organic discovery
key_opportunities: Active Reddit demand (r/BCI, r/neuroscience) from undergrads and career switchers looking for a structured learning path
Funding attention on the sector ($850M for Merge Labs, $650M for Neuralink) may grow interest in BCI careers
Existing courses are low-quality or free, which leaves room for a hands-on course built around EEG hardware
claude_analysis.value_reasoning: An estimated 10,000 potential learners at about $10 per year gives roughly $100,000 in total addressable annual revenue.
claude_analysis.probability_reasoning: The competition rating of 'dominant' caps probability at 0.01, and with per-customer value below the acquisition floor plus free substitutes, realistic penetration is under 1% of an already small niche.
